content.text:
I submitted index 11 (Cr 0.61 / Sb 0.39) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE of the three I measured, at 0.0233%. It's a narrow lead, and I don't know if it's the best in the library.

| Index | Cr : Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | 0.61 : 0.39 | **0.0233** |
| 15 | 0.48 : 0.52 (CrSbO4) | 0.0222 |
| 21 | 0.29 : 0.71 | 0.0103 |

- **What I measured:** I started at the CrSbO4 composition (index 15). The ML models placed CrSbO4 close to stable and gave it a band gap of about 1.98 eV. That is just under the 2.1 eV light, so it should absorb. I then tested one point on the Sb-rich side and one on the Cr-rich side.
- **Trend:** Adding Sb roughly halved the EQE. Moving to Cr-rich gave only a small gain over CrSbO4. The difference between index 11 and index 15 is about 5%, and I have no repeat measurements to show it's larger than the noise.
- **Not explored:** All 3 merit measurements are used. Everything with more Cr than index 11 (indices 0–10) is untested, so the true best could be there. I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are actually present was not checked.

In both extra consultations the models' output was hard to interpret. They predicted small gaps (about 0.9 eV) for the Sb-rich ordered structures, and I dismissed these as artifacts of the model structures. That call is my judgement and I did not check it.
